text: The Scandinavian Masters was an annual golf tournament on the European Tour held in Sweden. In 2020, it became co-sanctioned with the Ladies European Tour and was rebranded as the Scandinavian Mixed, in which both male and female golfers competed. The tournament originated from the Volvo Open and the Scandinavian Enterprise Open, which, in 1973, became the first Swedish stop on the European Tour schedule. In 1991, the Scandinavian Enterprise Open merged with the PLM Open, resulting in the tournament being named the Scandinavian Masters. It was generally the only European Tour event held in Scandinavia, and in 2013 had a prize fund of €1,500,000, which was at the lower end of the scale for European Tour events in the tour's home continent. Until 2011, it was played at the end of July or the beginning of August. In 2012, it moved to the first weekend in June and was played from Wednesday to Saturday to allow players more time to travel to the following week's U.S. Open. From 2013 to 2017, it was held in late May/early June, two weeks before the U.S. Open, but in 2018 it was played in August. In 2019, Lagardère Group passed management of the tournament to the European Tour, which renamed it the Scandinavian Invitation. In 2020, the European Tour and Ladies European Tour created the Scandinavian Mixed hosted by Henrik and Annika, bringing 78 men and 78 women together to compete in the same tournament for the same prize money, but playing from different tees. Official World Golf Ranking points were offered for both tours, along with points toward the European Tour's and LET's season-long competitions, as well as Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup points, if applicable, which required the results to be divided between men and women. The first event was originally scheduled for June 2020 but was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It returned in June 2021, with Jonathan Caldwell winning the inaugural mixed event by shooting a final-round 64 to beat Adrián Otaegui by one shot; Alice Hewson finished in third place as the highest-placed female. In 2022, Linn Grant became the first woman to win on the European Tour, winning by nine strokes ahead of Henrik Stenson and Marc Warren, with Gabriella Cowley in second place, 14 strokes behind; Linn Grant won again in 2024, beating Calum Hill and Sebastian Söderberg by one shot. The 2024 event was the final edition of the tournament, and in October 2024 it was confirmed that the tournament would not return in 2025.
